structure:
workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/prototype-specs is a small Playwright project that walks the Design Release 2.1 prototype (GB-notification-service at c2078fb, mounted at /design-release-2.1) and records a trace per test. playwright.config.js runs only e2e/**/*.fit.spec.js, one worker. In scope: the 12 fit specs that drove trace:prototype-dr2-1 (156 tests, all passing on 27 November 2026; index.json of traces-prototype lists the same 12 specs with the same counts): about-the-consignment (22 tests, 440 lines), description-of-the-goods (13, 362), transport-and-arrival (13, 373), documents (7, 144), consignment-parties (14, 454), address-book (9, 239), journeys (9, 417), eudpa-691 (4, 83), dashboard (9, 306), manage-notifications (7, 214), templates (12, 206) and snagging (37, 557); the shared helpers they assert through, e2e/support/journey.js (283 lines: page actions and shared assertions), fixtures.js (48), evidence.js (65) and snagging.js (63); and COVERAGE.md (249 lines: the route table, the 39 DR2.1 override views and whether each was visited, what could not be reached and why, and the numbered behaviour notes), with README.md (66) and playwright.config.js (52) for how the suite runs. Out of scope: e2e/wod-capture/ (7 *.capture.spec.js files under their own config, not matched by the fit config and absent from the trace index), explore/ (ad hoc exploration scripts and their dumps), the runner scripts (run-suite.js, collect-traces.js, gen-coverage.js, serve-prototype.js, global-setup.js), package files, playwright-report/ and test-results/. Cut one part per feature area in journey order, the end-to-end and dashboard areas after the section pages, the snag-list spec on its own, and COVERAGE.md as its own part. journey.js is read by every spec part, and each part claims only the shared assertions its own tests call.

Extracted in 10 parts:
Part 1, Section 1: about the consignment: Part 1 read in full e2e/about-the-consignment.fit.spec.js (440 lines, 22 tests in 5 describes), e2e/support/journey.js (283 lines) and e2e/support/fixtures.js (48 lines). The spec opens with three copy tables (REASON_HINTS, INTERNAL_MARKET_PURPOSES, and later GERMINAL_REASON_HINTS, GERMINAL_PURPOSE_HINTS, GERMINAL_SEMEN_RESULTS) and then walks section 1 of the task list in journey order: 'notification type' (3 tests: /create-notification redirect to /notification-type with its five options, Continue-with-nothing error and live animals to origin with a GBN-AG draft reference; category dashboard Create new skipping the question; plants for planting reaching an empty commodity search), 'origin of the import' (4 tests: page copy and buttons; region-code Yes reveal, empty-code error and country prefix; country optional with answers kept; country autocomplete), 'what are you importing' (5 tests: page copy, buttons, cancel and help details; nothing-selected error; cattle search results and selection panel; several commodities and Clear all; save and return to overview without validating), 'main import reason' (7 tests: five reasons with hints; reason optional; internal market purposes and error; transhipment destination country; transit port of exit and destination country; temporary admission horses exit date, real-date error and port of exit; the /prototype/reason-for-import seed route) and 'germinal products: section 1' (3 tests: germinal dashboard Create new to origin with the germinal status strip; germinal commodity search for semen and embryos with selection; germinal reasons and purposes with their hints, errors and onward route to /consignment-details). journey.js gives the /design-release-2.1 mount, the error-summary, inline-error, back-link and draft-reference assertions, the action-button values, the autocomplete, commodity-search and date-picker helpers, the SPECIES fixtures and the startNotification, answerOrigin, answerCommodity and answerReason steps; only what these tests call is claimed here. fixtures.js only records each test's visited pages for the trace index, so it yields no product claim. The part stops at /consignment-details, which part 2 covers.
Part 2, Section 2: description of the goods: Part 2 read e2e/description-of-the-goods.fit.spec.js in full (362 lines, 13 tests in 4 describes), plus e2e/support/journey.js (283 lines) and e2e/support/fixtures.js (48 lines) for the shared assertions and journey steps those tests call. The spec covers section 2 of the task list, 'Description of the goods'. Describe 'commodity details' (3 tests): cattle number of animals validation, two commodities and removing them, germinal quantity/packages/temperature. Describe 'total gross weight' (2 tests): the germinal-only weight page and its absence for live animals. Describe 'identification details' (6 tests): cattle per-animal identifiers saved one at a time, three species-specific identifier sets (horse, cat, pig) from one loop, poultry flock panel, germinal donor/dates/mark with errors. Describe 'additional details' (2 tests): cattle certification purpose and unweaned animals, poultry certification purpose only. Routes covered, under the /design-release-2.1 mount: /create-notification?category=germinal-products, /consignment-details, /what-are-you-importing, /consignment-gross-weight, /animal-identification-details, /additional-animal-details and /arrival-details as the onward page. Shared assertions used: expectHeading (first h1), expectErrorSummary ('There is a problem' title and exact linked messages in order), expectInlineError (.govuk-error-message), expectBackLink (.govuk-back-link href), saveAndContinue (button name=action value=continue). fixtures.js only records visited pages for the trace index, so it adds no product claims.
Part 3, Transport, arrival and documents: Part 3, Transport, arrival and documents. Read in full: e2e/transport-and-arrival.fit.spec.js (373 lines, 13 tests in 5 describes: arrival details 2, transit countries 1, transporter details 4, germinal transporter details 1, add a transporter 5), e2e/documents.fit.spec.js (144 lines, 7 tests in 2 describes: upload documents 6, upload documents from the hub 1), and the shared helpers e2e/support/journey.js (283 lines) and e2e/support/fixtures.js (48 lines). Pages covered, all under the /design-release-2.1 mount: /arrival-details, /transit-countries (and its guard), /transporter (list, selected, change, remove, germinal variant), the legacy /transport-details redirect, /transporter/add, /transporter/add/private (postcode, address results, details, manual entry, cancel), /transporter/add/commercial (authorisation number, Northern Ireland postcode, manual entry), /upload-documents (guidance, fields, validation, listing, virus status), /upload-documents/<id>/delete, and /upload-documents?from=hub. Shared journey.js assertions these tests call are claimed once each (error summary title, inline error, back link, heading, date format, start of a notification, arrival answers). fixtures.js only records visited pages for the trace index and shows no prototype behaviour.
Part 4, Consignment parties: Part 4, Consignment parties. Read in full: e2e/consignment-parties.fit.spec.js (455 lines, 14 tests in 5 describes), e2e/support/journey.js (283 lines: the URL helpers, action buttons, error summary and back-link assertions, the toRoles set-up steps, CORE_ADDRESSES, chooseAddress and fillCph) and e2e/support/fixtures.js (48 lines: records the pages each test visits; asserts nothing). Describes: 'consignment addresses' (8 tests: the cattle roles page, the cat roles page, picking an address for every role plus the CPH number page, remove, the same-as shortcuts, the picker search, a picker continued empty, save and return to hub), 'add an address from the journey' (2 tests: place of origin entered by hand, consignee found by UK postcode), 'add-address pages for the other roles' (1 test over consignor, importer and place of destination), 'permanent address' (2 tests: the per-animal page for cats, the retired enter-address path) and 'contact address for consignment' (1 test: it redirects to the review). Routes covered, all under /design-release-2.1: /roles-and-addresses, /place-of-origin, /consignor-or-exporter, /consignee, /importer, /place-of-destination, /<role>/add-address, /<role>/find-address, /<role>/find-address/select, /cph-number, /permanent-address, /permanent-address/select, /permanent-address/enter-address, /contact-address-for-consignment. Claims run in test order, then shared helper claims, then gaps.
Part 5, Address book: Part 5, Address book. Read in full: e2e/address-book.fit.spec.js (239 lines; 3 describes, 9 tests: 'address book list' with 1 test 'categories, pagination and filters' in 7 steps; 'add an address to the address book' with 6 tests: choose an address type, origin or consignor entered by hand, destination/consignee/importer found by postcode, branch, transporter hand-over, usage-step guard; 'an address book entry' with 2 tests: view/edit/save in 4 steps, and delete), e2e/support/journey.js (283 lines; this part claims only the shared helpers the address-book tests call: url/urlFor for the /design-release-2.1 mount, expectHeading on the first h1, expectErrorSummary with its 'There is a problem' title and exact ordered message list, expectBackLink, submitForm and clickAction) and e2e/support/fixtures.js (48 lines; records each test's main-frame navigations for the trace index, which is suite tooling and no prototype behaviour, so it gets no claim). Routes covered: /address-book (list, ?category=, ?page=2, search and type filter), /address-book/add, /address-book/add/lookup (and ?manual=true), /address-book/add/find-address, /address-book/add/find-address/select, /address-book/add/usage (guard only), /transporter/add (hand-over only), /address-book/<entry>, /address-book/<entry>/edit and /address-book/<entry>/delete.
Part 6, End-to-end journeys and the hub: Part 6 read four files in full: e2e/journeys.fit.spec.js (9 tests in 2 describes: 'notification journeys end to end' runs 5 table-driven walks — cattle by air, poultry by rail, pet cats by air, horse by sea, germinal bovine semen — from Create new to Import notification submitted, through the hub, review and declaration; 'the notification hub' has 4 tests: fresh hub all To do, hub task link returns to hub, review with tasks missing, submitted page guard), e2e/eudpa-691.fit.spec.js (4 tests: A1 Back in the opening run, A2 Arrival details from the hub returns to the hub, B1 and B2 Transit countries saved with none added, in the run and from the hub), and the shared helpers e2e/support/journey.js (base path, urlFor, step helpers, species, addresses, field names) and e2e/support/fixtures.js (records visited pages per test; no journey behaviour). Claims cover the page order each walk asserts, the hub rows, statuses and links, the review sections and content, the declaration copy and error, the submitted page copy and links, and every field and option the shared helpers drive for these tests.
Part 7, Dashboards and managing notifications: Part 7 read in full: e2e/dashboard.fit.spec.js (306 lines, 9 tests in 3 describes: overall dashboard (3 tests: the overall dashboard at the mount root, the /dashboard redirect, the prototype index), category dashboards (3 tests: live animals tabs, search, filters and cards; live animals filtered results; germinal products), at a glance drill-downs (3 tests: /actions, /changes, /inspection)); e2e/manage-notifications.fit.spec.js (214 lines, 7 tests in 5 describes: view a notification from the dashboard (2 tests: submitted with action required and its Actions menu; submitted, past and draft), amend a submitted notification (2 tests: confirm, change, save and return, resubmit; cancel an amendment), amend and copy guards (1 test), copy as new (1 test), delete a notification (1 test)); e2e/support/journey.js (283 lines; these specs call url, urlFor, expectHeading, expectBackLink, clickAction, submitForm, pickFromAutocomplete, fillDate and dateFromToday) and e2e/support/fixtures.js (48 lines; an auto fixture that records each test's main-frame navigations for the trace index, test tooling with nothing a user observes). Claims follow the specs in file order: overall dashboard, prototype index, category dashboards (cards, tabs, search, sort, filters, filtered results), the three drill-downs, then the review page per status, its Actions menu, amend confirm, amend review and save and return, resubmission, cancel amend, guards, copy as new and delete, then the shared journey.js mechanics these tests rest on. All paths are under /design-release-2.1. Gaps record what the covers ask for that these tests do not assert: drill-down table columns, make-template's destination, and guards for delete and make-template.
Part 8, Templates: Part 8, Templates. Read in full: e2e/templates.fit.spec.js (206 lines, 12 tests in 3 describes: 'manage templates' 2 tests, 'a saved template' 6 tests, 'create a new template' 4 tests, the first of which has 5 steps), e2e/support/journey.js (283 lines) and e2e/support/fixtures.js (48 lines, which only records each test's navigations into test-results/meta and asserts nothing). Covered: the manage templates list at /templates and the dashboard's Use template button; a saved template's view page (/templates/<slug>), its use (/use), edit (/edit), change-one-section (/change/<page>), delete confirmation (/delete), the POST-reloads and unknown-slug redirects; creating a template (notification type, /templates/create name page, origin and commodity in template mode, the documents and declaration redirects, review and save), saving with no name (/templates/save) and discarding (/templates/discard) inside and outside a template journey. Shared journey.js assertions these tests call and that are claimed here: the /design-release-2.1 mount (url, urlFor), expectHeading (first h1), expectBackLink (.govuk-back-link href), saveAndContinue (button action=continue), submitForm (named main button), answerOrigin and answerCommodity with SPECIES.cattle. The rest of journey.js belongs to other parts.
Part 9, Live-animals snag list: Part 9, the live-animals snag list. Read in full: e2e/snagging.fit.spec.js (557 lines, 37 tests in 12 describes, S01 to S38 with S30 left out), e2e/support/snagging.js (63 lines: shoot, shootNoJs, shootMobile screenshot helpers), e2e/support/journey.js (283 lines: URL helpers, journey step helpers and the species and address fixtures) and e2e/support/fixtures.js (48 lines: the visited-pages recorder). Each snag test walks the live-animals journey to the page state a designer snag is about and takes full-page screenshots (desktop, and where named, with JavaScript off or at phone width). Most tests assert little beyond reaching the page; the claims record each page state reached, every selector, label, option, copy string and branch the tests assert or drive, and the snag number. Describes covered: origin of the import (S01-S05), what are you importing (S06-S08), main import reason (S09-S12), commodity details (S13-S14), identification details (S15-S18), arrival details (S19-S23), transit countries (S24-S25), transporter details (S26-S27), upload documents (S28, S29, S31), consignment addresses (S32, S33, S36, S37), review your notification (S34, S35) and notification submitted (S38). From the shared journey.js only the helpers this spec calls are claimed; the germinal helpers, the error-summary and back-link assertions and the reference reader are other parts' to claim.
Part 10, COVERAGE.md and suite set-up: Part 10 read COVERAGE.md in full (header, the generated Routes table of 77 GET routes under /design-release-2.1, the 39-row DR2.1 override views table, 'Not reached, and why' with 9 items, and 'Behaviour worth knowing' with 19 numbered items), README.md in full (run instructions, outputs, layout, prototype gotchas), playwright.config.js and e2e/support/evidence.js. Claims cover: the suite's baseline (prototype commit, 156 passing tests); one claim per route row (route, view, override or shared, visited or not); one claim per override-view row; one gap per unreached route or behaviour with its reason; one or more claims per numbered behaviour item (13 marked observed, not asserted); the README gotchas that describe prototype behaviour (arrival date window, bespoke autocompletes, species checkboxes, MOJ date picker, session racing, dev mode); and the suite set-up that bounds what it can reach (one worker, chromium at 1280x1200, trace and video on every test, evidence slugs). Spec behaviour behind each route is claimed by the spec parts.

claims.statement: Every Design Release 2.1 page is served under the /design-release-2.1 path, a mirror of the root route table.
claims.quote:
// Design Release 2.1 is a mirror mount of the root route table.
const BASE = '/design-release-2.1'

claims.statement: Going to /create-notification with no category redirects to /notification-type.
claims.ref: e2e/about-the-consignment.fit.spec.js:36-38 (notification type > create new asks what is being imported before the journey starts)
claims.quote:
await page.goto(url('/create-notification'))
      await expect(page).toHaveURL(urlFor('/notification-type'))

claims.statement: The notification type page's title is 'What are you importing? - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
claims.quote: await expect(page).toHaveTitle('What are you importing? - Import notification service - GOV.UK')

claims.statement: The notification type question is a fieldset legend h1 reading 'What are you importing?' with the caption 'About the consignment'.
claims.quote: await expect(page.locator('legend h1')).toHaveText(/About the consignment\s+What are you importing\?/)

claims.statement: The notification type question offers five radio options, in order: 'Live animals', 'Germinal products (semen, ova, embryos)', 'Plants for planting', 'Potatoes (seed and ware)', 'Wood products'.
claims.quote:
await expect(page.locator('input[name="notificationType"] + label')).toHaveText([
        'Live animals',
        'Germinal products (semen, ova, embryos)',
        'Plants for planting',
        'Potatoes (seed and ware)',
        'Wood products'
      ])

claims.statement: The notification type page's back link goes to the Design Release 2.1 root (/design-release-2.1).
claims.quote: await expectBackLink(page, url())

claims.statement: The notification type page has one action button, 'Continue'.
claims.quote: await expect(page.locator('button[name="action"]')).toHaveText(['Continue'])

claims.statement: Continuing from the notification type page with nothing chosen shows the error summary message 'Select what you are importing', linked to #notificationType.
claims.quote:
await expectErrorSummary(page, ['Select what you are importing'])
      await expectInlineError(page, 'Select what you are importing')
      await expect(page.locator('.govuk-error-summary__list a')).toHaveAttribute('href', '#notificationType')

claims.statement: The 'Select what you are importing' error is also shown inline on the notification type question.
claims.quote: await expectInlineError(page, 'Select what you are importing')

claims.statement: Choosing 'Live animals' and continuing opens /origin-of-the-import.
claims.quote:
await page.locator('input[name="notificationType"][value="live-animals"]').check()
      await saveAndContinue(page)
      await expect(page).toHaveURL(urlFor('/origin-of-the-import'))

claims.statement: Once the notification type is chosen, the notification has a draft reference of the form GBN-AG-26- followed by capital letters and digits, shown on the origin page.
claims.quote: expect(await readReference(page)).toMatch(/^GBN-AG-26-[A-Z0-9]+$/)

claims.statement: Journey pages show a draft strip with the status 'Draft' and the notification reference.
claims.quote:
/** The draft strip (status tag + notification reference) on journey pages. */
await expect(page.locator('main')).toContainText('Draft')

claims.statement: 'Create new' on the live animals dashboard (/live-animals) goes straight to /origin-of-the-import, skipping the notification type question.
claims.ref: e2e/about-the-consignment.fit.spec.js:70-73 (notification type > starting from a category dashboard skips the type question)
claims.quote:
await page.goto(url('/live-animals'))
    await page.locator('main').getByRole('button', { name: 'Create new' }).click()
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(urlFor('/origin-of-the-import'))

claims.statement: When the origin page is reached from the live animals dashboard, its back link goes to /live-animals rather than /notification-type.
claims.quote: await expectBackLink(page, url('/live-animals'))

claims.statement: Choosing 'Plants for planting' leads through the origin page to /what-are-you-importing, the same commodity search page as live animals.
claims.quote:
await startNotification(page, 'plants-for-planting')
    await answerOrigin(page)
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(urlFor('/what-are-you-importing'))

claims.statement: For a plants for planting notification the commodity search offers nothing to pick: typing 'cattle' shows no species checkboxes.
claims.quote:
test('plants for planting reaches the commodity search, which offers nothing to pick'
    await input.pressSequentially('cattle', { delay: 30 })
    await expect(page.locator('input[name="commodity-selection"]')).toHaveCount(0)
claims.note: The test searches only 'cattle', an animal term; it does not try a plant name, so 'nothing to pick' rests on the title. The locator checks input[name="commodity-selection"], a different name from the species checkboxes the other tests tick (#commodity-species-...).

claims.statement: The suite does not walk the 'Germinal products', 'Potatoes (seed and ware)' or 'Wood products' options of the notification type question beyond their labels, so what each leads to is unproven here; germinal products is reached only through its dashboard and the category query.
The origin page's title is 'Origin of the import - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
claims.ref: e2e/about-the-consignment.fit.spec.js:95 (origin of the import > renders the origin questions)
claims.quote: await expect(page).toHaveTitle('Origin of the import - Import notification service - GOV.UK')

claims.statement: The origin page's h1 is 'Origin of the import'.
claims.quote: await expectHeading(page, 'Origin of the import')

claims.statement: The origin page shows the section caption 'About the consignment'.
claims.quote: await expect(main).toContainText('About the consignment')

claims.statement: The origin page has a 'Country of origin' heading.
claims.quote: await expect(main.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Country of origin' })).toBeVisible()

claims.statement: The country of origin field is a search box with the placeholder 'Search for a country'.
claims.quote: await expect(page.locator('#country-of-origin')).toHaveAttribute('placeholder', 'Search for a country')

claims.statement: The origin page asks 'Does the consignment have a region of origin code?'.
claims.quote: await expect(main).toContainText('Does the consignment have a region of origin code?')

claims.statement: The region of origin code question has the hint 'Check the health certificate for a region of origin code. You can add the code later if you do not have the certificate now.'
claims.quote: await expect(main).toContainText('Check the health certificate for a region of origin code. You can add the code later if you do not have the certificate now.')

claims.statement: The region of origin code question is a Yes/No radio (regionOfOriginRequired, values 'Yes' and 'No').
claims.quote:
await page.locator('input[name="regionOfOriginRequired"][value="Yes"]').check()
await page.locator('input[name="regionOfOriginRequired"][value="No"]').check()

claims.statement: The origin page has a field labelled 'Your internal reference for this consignment (optional)'.
claims.quote: await expect(page.getByLabel('Your internal reference for this consignment (optional)')).toBeVisible()

claims.statement: The internal reference field has the hint 'Enter any internal reference you want to use to identify this consignment, or leave blank.'
claims.quote: await expect(main).toContainText('Enter any internal reference you want to use to identify this consignment, or leave blank.')

claims.statement: When reached from the notification type question, the origin page's back link goes to /notification-type.
claims.quote: await expectBackLink(page, url('/notification-type'))

claims.statement: The origin page offers only one action button, 'Save and continue': there is no 'Save and return to overview' button.
claims.quote:
// DR2.1 origin offers only the forward button: no hub save, no cancel link.
    await expect(page.locator('button[name="action"]')).toHaveText(['Save and continue'])

claims.statement: The origin page has no 'Cancel and return to overview' link.
claims.quote: await expect(main.getByRole('link', { name: 'Cancel and return to overview' })).toHaveCount(0)

claims.statement: The region of origin code box is hidden until 'Yes' is chosen for the region of origin code question.
claims.ref: e2e/about-the-consignment.fit.spec.js:113-116 (origin of the import > region code: Yes reveals the code box ...)
claims.quote:
await expect(page.locator('#region-of-origin-code-suffix')).toBeHidden()
      await page.locator('input[name="regionOfOriginRequired"][value="Yes"]').check()
      await expect(page.getByLabel('Enter the region of origin code')).toBeVisible()

claims.statement: The revealed region code box is labelled 'Enter the region of origin code'.
claims.quote: await expect(page.getByLabel('Enter the region of origin code')).toBeVisible()

claims.statement: The region code box has the hint 'Enter up to 5 characters.'
claims.quote: await expect(page.locator('main')).toContainText('Enter up to 5 characters.')

claims.statement: Choosing 'Yes' for the region code and leaving the code empty shows the error summary message 'Enter the region of origin code', linked to #region-of-origin-code-suffix.
claims.quote:
await expectErrorSummary(page, ['Enter the region of origin code'])
      await expect(page.locator('.govuk-error-summary__list a')).toHaveAttribute('href', '#region-of-origin-code-suffix')

claims.statement: The 'Enter the region of origin code' error is also shown inline on the code box.
claims.quote: await expectInlineError(page, 'Enter the region of origin code')

claims.statement: The chosen country of origin's two-letter code is shown as a fixed prefix in front of the region code box: picking France shows 'FR'.
claims.quote:
await pickFromAutocomplete(page, 'country-of-origin', 'Fran', 'France')
      await expect(page.locator('#region-of-origin-code-prefix')).toHaveText('FR')

claims.statement: With a country, 'Yes' and a region code ('75') entered, Save and continue goes to /what-are-you-importing.
claims.quote:
await page.locator('#region-of-origin-code-suffix').fill('75')
      await capture(page, testInfo, 'region-code-prefix')
      await saveAndContinue(page)
      await expect(page).toHaveURL(urlFor('/what-are-you-importing'))

claims.statement: No test enters a region code longer than 5 characters or with invalid characters, so whether 'Enter up to 5 characters.' is enforced, and its error message, is unproven.
A country of origin is not needed to continue: with no country, 'No' for the region code and an internal reference, Save and continue goes to /what-are-you-importing.
claims.ref: e2e/about-the-consignment.fit.spec.js:139-143 (origin of the import > country is optional to proceed and the answers are kept)
claims.quote:
await page.locator('input[name="regionOfOriginRequired"][value="No"]').check()
    await page.locator('#internal-reference').fill('REF-2026/01')
    await saveAndContinue(page)
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(urlFor('/what-are-you-importing'))

claims.statement: Returning to the origin page shows the saved answers: the region code 'No' radio is checked and the internal reference keeps 'REF-2026/01'.
claims.quote:
await page.goto(url('/origin-of-the-import'))
    await expect(page.locator('input[name="regionOfOriginRequired"][value="No"]')).toBeChecked()
    await expect(page.locator('#internal-reference')).toHaveValue('REF-2026/01')

claims.statement: A country of origin left empty stays empty when the origin page is revisited.
claims.quote: await expect(page.locator('input[name="countryOfOrigin"]')).toHaveValue('')

claims.statement: The internal reference accepts letters, digits, a hyphen and a slash ('REF-2026/01'), inferred because the value is saved without error and shown again.
claims.quote: await page.locator('#internal-reference').fill('REF-2026/01')
claims.note: No test sets a length limit or character rule for the internal reference.

claims.statement: Typing part of a country name ('Neth') in the country of origin search shows matching countries as options, including 'Netherlands'.
claims.ref: e2e/about-the-consignment.fit.spec.js:150-154 (origin of the import > the country search offers matching countries and keeps the pick)
claims.quote:
await input.pressSequentially('Neth', { delay: 30 })
    await expect(page.locator('button.app-country-search__option', { hasText: 'Netherlands' })).toBeVisible()

claims.statement: Picking a country option stores the country's name ('Netherlands') as the country of origin answer.
claims.quote:
await page.locator('button.app-country-search__option', { hasText: 'Netherlands' }).click()
    await expect(page.locator('input[name="countryOfOrigin"]')).toHaveValue('Netherlands')

claims.statement: The country of origin search is a bespoke type-and-pick autocomplete that redraws its options on each key typed; clicking an option writes the hidden value the server reads.
claims.quote:
* Bespoke type-and-pick autocompletes (country of origin, port of entry, transit
 * country). They render on each input event, so type per key, then click the

// Design Release 2.1 is a mirror mount of the root route table.
const BASE = '/design-release-2.1'

claims.statement: Description of the goods is section 2 of the task list and holds commodity details, identification details and additional details; which pages appear depends on the species chosen.
claims.quote:
// Section 2 of the DR2.1 task list: commodity details, identification details
// and additional details. Which pages appear depends on the species chosen.

claims.statement: After the reason for import page, a live animals notification lands on the commodity details page at /consignment-details.
claims.quote:
await answerReason(page, reason)
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(urlFor('/consignment-details'))

claims.statement: A germinal products notification can be started directly at /create-notification?category=germinal-products, and then goes through origin, commodity search and reason to commodity details.
claims.quote:
if (type === 'germinal-products') {
    await page.goto(url('/create-notification?category=germinal-products'))
claims.note: The helper goes straight on to answerOrigin, so the category query appears to skip the notification type page; the test does not assert the URL after the goto.

claims.statement: The commodity details page has the title 'Commodity details - Import notification service - GOV.UK' and the heading 'Commodity details'.
claims.quote:
await expect(page).toHaveTitle('Commodity details - Import notification service - GOV.UK')
      await expectHeading(page, 'Commodity details')

claims.statement: The commodity details page shows the section caption 'Description of the goods'.
claims.quote: await expect(main).toContainText('Description of the goods')

claims.statement: The commodity details page lists the 'Selected commodities' in a table with columns Commodity code, Commodity and Species; for cattle the row reads 0102, Cattle, Domestic cattle (Bos taurus).

await expect(main).toContainText('Selected commodities')
      await expect(main).toContainText(/Commodity code\s+Commodity\s+Species\s+0102\s+Cattle\s+Domestic cattle \(Bos taurus\)/)

claims.statement: Each selected commodity on the commodity details page has a 'Remove' button.

claims.statement: The commodity details page has an 'Add another commodity' link back to the commodity search at /what-are-you-importing.

claims.statement: For a live animal commodity, the commodity details page shows a block headed with the commodity name and code, such as 'Cattle (0102)'.
claims.quote: await expect(main).toContainText('Cattle (0102)')

claims.statement: For live animals, each commodity block asks for 'Number of animals'.
claims.quote: await expect(page.getByLabel('Number of animals')).toBeVisible()

claims.statement: For live animals, each commodity block has an optional field labelled 'Number of packages (when required)' with the hint 'Such as crates, bags or boxes'.
claims.quote:
await expect(page.getByLabel('Number of packages (when required)')).toBeVisible()
      await expect(main).toContainText('Such as crates, bags or boxes')
claims.note: The test continues with only the number of animals filled, so packages are not required for live animals.

claims.statement: The commodity details page's back link goes to the commodity search at /what-are-you-importing, for live animals and germinal products.
claims.quote: await expectBackLink(page, url('/what-are-you-importing'))

claims.statement: Continuing with no number of animals shows the error 'Enter the number of animals' in a 'There is a problem' error summary, linked to the field with id number-of-animals-<species id> (for cattle, #number-of-animals-cattle-bos-taurus).

await expectErrorSummary(page, ['Enter the number of animals'])
      await expect(page.locator('.govuk-error-summary__list a')).toHaveAttribute('href', '#number-of-animals-cattle-bos-taurus')

      await expectErrorSummary(page, ['Enter a whole number greater than 0'])
